name: Mixed Germ Cell Tumor of Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Histological identification of mixed germ cell tumor components including embryonal carcinoma, yolk sac tumor, choriocarcinoma, and teratoma
MRI showing a heterogeneously enhancing mass in typical CNS midline locations such as pineal or suprasellar regions
Elevated cerebrospinal fluid or serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and/or beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG)
Symptoms consistent with CNS mass effect such as headache, nausea, and endocrine dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of mixed germ cell tumor components plus supportive imaging and tumor marker elevation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology, imaging, and tumor marker data due to heterogeneous tumor composition.

pathognomonic.notes: Commonly associated with pineal region tumors
searchTerms: difficulty moving eyes up and down

pathognomonic.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic-pituitary axis involvement
pathognomonic.notes: Includes diabetes insipidus and precocious puberty
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage

common.symptomName: Headache due to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain from increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting secondary to intracranial hypertension
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from brain pressure
vomiting due to increased intracranial pressure
walking problems from brain fluid buildup

rare.symptomName: Cranial nerve palsies other than vertical gaze palsy
searchTerms: weakness of facial or eye muscles
cranial nerve weakness except vertical gaze

laboratory: Elevated serum and CSF beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG)
CSF cytology may show malignant germ cell components
imaging: MRI revealing heterogeneously enhancing mass in pineal or suprasellar region
Hydrocephalus due to obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid pathways
T1 hypointense and T2 hyperintense lesion with cystic and solid components
genetic: No consistent germline mutations; somatic mutations may include KIT and KRAS alterations
other: Histopathology demonstrating mixed germ cell tumor components
Immunohistochemistry positive for placental alkaline phosphatase (PLAP), AFP, and β-hCG

distinguishingFeatures: Typically normal or mildly elevated AFP and β-hCG
Better prognosis and different treatment protocols
Primitive neuroectodermal tumor with different histology
No elevation of germ cell tumor markers

redFlags: Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as papilledema
Endocrine abnormalities indicating hypothalamic-pituitary axis involvement
references: Louis DN, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021.
Müller HL. Central Nervous System Germ Cell Tumors: Diagnosis and Treatment. Expert Rev Neurother. 2018.
